te: Issues prepared for discussion with the Minister of Defence, and approaches to building warships in Thailand heard
se: The meeting set issues for discussion with the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Defence, such as improving laws, investment incentives and research and development, and heard information from the Defence Industry Association that Thailand has the capacity to build its own frigates, which would reduce dependence on other countries and create jobs. It proposed that the state have a clear and continuous policy to support domestic industry
it: Issues for discussion with the Minister of Defence (13 November 2024)
Approaches to promoting the building of large warships in Thailand

te: Examples of projects that can grow the defence industry, such as counter-drone systems, studied
se: The meeting considered information to set approaches to promoting the defence industry, studying examples of projects that can be built upon, such as counter-unmanned aircraft systems made in Thailand, which can be used both for national defence and to help with disaster relief
it: Examples of projects that can grow the defence industry

te: Defence policy and Thailand's shipbuilding capacity heard
se: The meeting noted the plan for a courtesy call on the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Defence, and heard the Ministry of Defence's policy on developing the defence industry, equipment readiness, digital technology and a cyber force, as well as information on Thailand's shipbuilding capacity, such as offshore patrol vessels and frigates, obstacles in personnel and law, and industry groups that deserve priority, such as space, cyber, aircraft and armoured vehicles
it: The Ministry of Defence's policy on the defence industry and digital technology
Shipbuilding capacity and milestones for the defence industry

te: Meeting 2/2567 · Subcommittee on Cyber, Technology, Weapons and Defence Industry (2024–2025 term)
First meeting: approaches set for promoting research, military equipment, cyber and space
se: The meeting considered how to work to promote, and remove obstacles to, research and development of weapons, military equipment, cyber, space and security industry technology, so that it benefits the country and the people sustainably, and considered appointing experts as advisers, for submission to the committee
it: The subcommittee's working approach
Appointment of advisers to the subcommittee

te: Timing set for submitting 2 reports, and a study of migrant workers and security begun
se: The meeting noted its work plan and set the period for submitting draft study reports on the area of overlapping claims between Thailand and Cambodia around Ko Kut, Trat Province, and on the repeal of the Internal Security Act B.E. 2551 (2008), during the session from 12 December 2024 to 10 April 2025. It approved the work frameworks of all 3 working groups, and approved preparing a framework for a study of migrant workers and national security, inviting the Office of the National Security Council and the Ministry of Public Health to give information
it: Timing set for submitting the draft reports on Ko Kut and on the internal security law
Work frameworks of 3 working groups
Study of migrant workers and national security

te: Outline of the Ko Kut report approved, and a briefing on the internal security law heard
se: The meeting forwarded a letter from local administrative organisations in the southern border provinces requesting budget support to the committee concerned, approved the outline of the study report on the area of overlapping claims between Thailand and Cambodia around Ko Kut, Trat Province, asking for information to be completed, heard a briefing on the Internal Security Act B.E. 2551 (2008), and approved proposing the appointment of additional advisers
it: Letter from local administrative organisations in the southern border provinces
Outline of the study report on the area of overlapping claims between Thailand and Cambodia around Ko Kut, Trat Province
Internal Security Act B.E. 2551 (2008)

te: Study of the internal security law begun, and a framework for studying Ko Kut
se: The meeting noted the schedule of site visits to the southern border provinces and a letter inviting it to hear views on peace in the southern border provinces, approved proposing the appointment of additional advisers, approved a plan to study the repeal of the Internal Security Act B.E. 2551 (2008), and approved a framework for studying the area of overlapping claims between Thailand and Cambodia around Ko Kut, Trat Province
it: Appointment of additional advisers to the subcommittee
Study of the repeal of the Internal Security Act B.E. 2551 (2008)
The area of overlapping claims between Thailand and Cambodia around Ko Kut, Trat Province

te: 3 working groups formed, and requests from local administrations in the southern border provinces followed up
se: The meeting approved sending letters to the Bureau of the Budget and the Department of Local Administration about a request for a specific-purpose grant from a subdistrict administrative organisation in the southern border provinces, formed 3 working groups (law reform, public relations and security innovation), and followed up site visits to the southern border provinces in response to a letter from a civil society network
it: Request for a specific-purpose grant from a local administrative organisation in the southern border provinces
Forming 3 working groups
Site visits to the southern border provinces

te: 3 roles set, and site visits to the southern border provinces prepared
se: The meeting noted the setting up of 3 subcommittees and the sending of representatives on a courtesy call on the Minister of Defence, and set 3 roles: helping to improve laws and regulations that are obstacles to maintaining security, publicising facts and knowledge about security, and proposing innovations to develop security in the 21st century. It also prepared site visits to the southern border provinces in coordination with local security agencies
it: Framework of 3 roles and goals for the subcommittee
Site visits to the southern border provinces

te: Year-end work summarised, and plans for the first quarter of 2025
se: The meeting summarised its work in November–December 2024, in which each working group is preparing a report expected to be completed between January and February 2025, and planned the first quarter of 2025, such as meeting every Wednesday, study visits to Chon Buri and the Government Lottery Office, and a forum on security research technology with academic institutions and the Royal Thai Army Command and General Staff College
it: Summary of work in November–December 2024
Work plan for quarter 1 of 2025 (meetings, study visits and forums)

te: 3 reports proposed: conscripts, reserve forces for disaster relief, and veterans' welfare
se: The meeting considered preparing 3 study reports for the committee: approaches to developing armed forces personnel in the case of conscripts, a framework for using reserve forces to help with disaster relief, and approaches to developing veterans' rights and welfare. It sent representatives to help prepare the committee's annual report, considered requesting a meeting with the Chief of Defence Forces on disaster management, and invited the Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation and the Army Personnel Department to give information
it: 3 study reports for the committee
The national disaster prevention and mitigation plan, and the selection of men for conscription
Requesting a meeting with the Chief of Defence Forces on disaster management

te: Situation on the northern border heard, and a study visit, a forum and an ordination project prepared
se: The meeting heard experts on the situation of armed groups along the northern border and proposed approaches to organising the border clearly. It set the schedule of a study visit to the East in January 2025 and a forum on new forms of threat, considered the project "Soldiers of the King: Ordination to Develop Thai Localities in Honour of His Majesty", to make merit in honour of His Majesty the King on the auspicious occasion of His Majesty's 6th Cycle Birthday Anniversary on 28 July 2024, and considered its study of the draft Act on the Organisation of the Ministry of Defence (No. ..) B.E. .... assigned by the committee
it: Situation along the northern border
Schedule of the study visit to the East and the forum on new forms of threat
The project "Soldiers of the King: Ordination to Develop Thai Localities in Honour of His Majesty"
Results of the study of the draft Act on the Organisation of the Ministry of Defence (No. ..) B.E. ....

te: Veterans' honour allowance and medical checks before conscription selection followed up
se: The meeting considered a letter from a veterans' association on following up the honour allowance, invited the Army Medical Department to give information on medical checks before the selection of men for conscription and the duties of the medical board, adjusted the reserve forces group's work plan, and set up a working group for the project "Soldiers of the King: Ordination to Develop Thai Localities in Honour of His Majesty"
it: Veterans' honour allowance
Medical checks before the selection of men for conscription
Working group for the project "Soldiers of the King: Ordination to Develop Thai Localities in Honour of His Majesty"

te: More working groups set up, and reserve forces and new-recruit training studied
se: The meeting set up additional working groups, noted the appointment of honorary advisers under the committee's resolution, considered reserve force affairs under the Territorial Defence Command, invited the Army Training Command to give information on new-recruit training, and adjusted the working groups' plans
it: Setting up working groups and appointing honorary advisers
Reserve force affairs of the Territorial Defence Command
The Royal Thai Army's new-recruit training

te: Incentives for military service and changes to the reserve forces law for disaster relief proposed
se: The meeting invited the Territorial Defence Command to give information on applications from men liable for service to serve as conscripts by request (special case) online, and proposed publicising benefits such as the right to sit the non-commissioned officer school examination, welfare and education, together with in-depth health checks to reduce losses during training. It invited the Defence Mobilisation Department to give information on the Reserve Forces Act B.E. 2558 (2015), proposing changes to laws, regulations and the chain of command so that reserve forces can really be used for disaster prevention and relief
it: Applications from men liable for service to serve as conscripts by request (special case) online
The Reserve Forces Act B.E. 2558 (2015) and related regulations
